# The Cognitive Dimensions: The 5-Stage Lifecycle and The Co-Design Matrix

![Systems Organ Focus: Tracing the complete cognitive lifecycle across the five sensory-motor stages, the multi-rate temporal hierarchy, and the Physical AI Co-Design Matrix.](figures/fig_pipeline_locator.svg){#fig-locator-ch03 width=100%}

Chapter 2 established the quantitative physical constraints and timing budgets. This chapter defines the computational work that must execute within those constraints.

An embodied agent must perceive 3D metric space, maintain temporal belief under occlusion, reason over open-world instructions, plan smooth multi-step trajectories, and execute motor setpoints under mathematical safety filters. It must perform this work across three temporal cadences on heterogeneous silicon. In this chapter, we establish the five cognitive rows of the Physical AI Co-Design Matrix, architect the three cadences that decouple high-level deliberation from trajectory decoding and bare-metal reflexes, and examine the architectural mechanisms that reconcile cognition with physical dynamics.

::: {.callout-objective}
By the conclusion of this chapter, you will be able to:

1. **Map the Embodied Cognitive Lifecycle:** Deconstruct an autonomous physical task into five canonical stages: spatial perception in $SE(3)$, temporal world modeling, semantic goal decomposition, trajectory planning with action chunks, and real-time safety enforcement.
2. **Architect Multi-Rate Cadences:** Decouple slow semantic deliberation ($0.5\text{ to } 2\text{ Hz}$) from intermediate trajectory decoding ($20\text{ to } 50\text{ Hz}$) and bare-metal safety reflexes ($1000\text{ Hz}$), distinguishing each tier by rate, determinism, memory model, and hardware authority.
3. **Formulate the Fundamental Systems Tension:** Analyze the structural conflict between high-capacity neural deliberation (demanding time, parameters, and memory) and physical dynamics (demanding microsecond determinism and fresh sensory evidence).
4. **Construct the Physical AI Co-Design Matrix:** Intersect the five cognitive obligations with the five physical constraint columns, identifying which interactions dominate system architecture and which are non-binding.
5. **Apply Three Architectural Contracts:** Implement proposal and permission privilege boundaries, action-chunk delay amortization, and expiring intent leases ($\mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}}$) to resolve the compute-versus-physics conflict without collapsing runtime cadences.
:::

::: {.callout-autopsy title="The Multi-Rate Timing Collapse"}
* **System:** High-speed dual-arm sorting manipulator ($2.2\text{ m/s}$ end-effector velocity, six-degree-of-freedom cycloidal joints) running a vision-language model and motor Field-Oriented Control within a shared host runtime.
* **Incident:** The left arm seized mid-trajectory while descending toward a moving conveyor. Phase currents desynchronized, and back-EMF spikes destroyed the DC bus capacitor bank.
* **Telemetry Snapshot:** Ambient lighting flicker and an occluded workpiece produced an out-of-distribution visual scene. Autoregressive reasoning inflated inference latency from a nominal $P_{50} = 420\text{ ms}$ to $1{,}850\text{ ms}$. Motor phase commutation in the shared asynchronous event loop stalled for approximately $1{,}400\text{ ms}$.
* **Root Cause:** The $20\text{ kHz}$ commutation loop and $1000\text{ Hz}$ trajectory interpolator were starved of CPU cycles because they shared an execution runtime with an unconstrained $1\text{ Hz}$ semantic deliberation engine.
* **Architectural Flaw:** Multi-rate collapse. Slow deliberation was not isolated from trajectory decoding and motor reflexes on independent, hardware-isolated silicon.
* **Provenance:** Engineered composite based on documented industrial failure classes; system parameters and costs are constructed for pedagogical clarity.
:::

{{< pagebreak >}}

::: {.callout-contract title="The Multi-Rate Proposal and Permission Contract"}
| Component | Substrate | Contract Specification |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **MPU Proposes (S2 / S1.5)** | Untrusted · Linux MPU / NPU | Emits intent lease $\mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}} = \langle \mathbf{T}_{\text{target}}, \mathcal{B}, \|\mathbf{v}\|_{\text{max}}, t_{\text{issue}}, \Delta t_{\text{TTL}} \rangle$; generates action chunk $\mathbf{A}_{t:t+H}$ ($H=16$ at $20\text{ to } 50\text{ Hz}$); asserts heartbeat $\tau_{\text{heartbeat}} \le 10\text{ ms}$. |
| **MCU Permits (S1)** | Trusted · Bare-Metal MCU | Audits sensory freshness ($\Delta t_{\text{evidence}} \le \tau_{\text{wall}}$); evaluates Control Barrier Function QP at $1000\text{ Hz}$; verifies stopping clearance ($d_{\text{stop}}(v) \le d_{\text{clear}}$); monitors hardware watchdog $\tau_{\text{watchdog}} = 20\text{ ms}$. |
| **Failure Escalation** | MCU Hardware Reflex | On heartbeat timeout ($t > 20\text{ ms}$) or expired intent lease, discard proposals and execute controlled Category 1 dynamic deceleration, followed by Safe Torque Off. |
:::

::: {.callout-note icon=false title="The Sim-to-Real Delta"}
**Simulation Synchrony vs. Bench Reality:**
Simulation environments frequently execute the complete agent within a single synchronous step loop (`obs = env.reset(); action = model(obs); env.step(action)`), as though the physical universe pauses during computation. On physical hardware, the world never pauses: neural foundation models require hundreds of milliseconds while inverters require microsecond switching; operating systems encounter preemption jitter and memory bus stalls; and video Direct Memory Access saturates shared memory crossbars.
:::

---

## What Computational Work Must an Embodied Agent Perform?

Digital machine learning processes digital inputs to produce digital outputs. A cloud language model can take an extra second to generate tokens without violating physical laws.

An embodied physical agent exists to alter the configuration of the physical world ($W_t \to W_{t+1}$) by delivering forces, torques, and velocities through physical actuators, subject to the freshness and stopping budgets established in Chapter 2. That computational workload decomposes into five foundational stages:

1. **Perceive:** Transform continuous sensory streams into compact, metric 3D spatial representations.
2. **Remember:** Maintain a persistent belief state that survives occlusions, sensor noise, and communication dropouts.
3. **Reason:** Deliberate over open-vocabulary instructions and decompose abstract goals into geometrically bounded sub-tasks.
4. **Plan:** Synthesize smooth, kinematically feasible multi-step trajectory chunks that respect obstacle clearances and jerk bounds.
5. **Execute:** Project candidate trajectory commands onto mathematical safety invariants at microsecond cadences, translating permitted signals into electromagnetic motor flux.

![The Complete End-to-End Physical Agent Lifecycle. Tracing dataflow from open-world goal ingestion through 3D spatial perception, latent world modeling, expiring intent leases, action chunk decoding, real-time safety projection, hardware PWM switching, and endogenous feedback mutation ($W_t \to W_{t+1} \to O_{t+1}$).](figures/fig03_agent_workflow.svg){#fig-agent-workflow width=100%}

### The 9 Stations of the Agent Dataflow

As illustrated in @fig-agent-workflow, an embodied task traverses nine concrete lifecycle stations across heterogeneous hardware domains:

1. **Station 1 (Goal Ingestion):** An operator or orchestration service transmits an open-vocabulary natural language command: *"Pick up the steel bracket from the jig and place it into the quench tank."*
2. **Station 2 (Physical Transduction):** Reflected photons integrate in CMOS photodiode arrays ($t_{\text{exp}} \approx 8\text{ ms}$). Hardware Direct Memory Access (DMA) engines serialize raw pixel streams across MIPI CSI-2 interfaces directly into DRAM ($t_{\text{dma}} \approx 3\text{ ms}$) without CPU intervention.
3. **Station 3 (3D Spatial Perception):** An edge Vision Transformer or self-supervised backbone (such as DINOv2) extracts visual features, unprojecting 2D pixels into metric 3D space using calibrated camera extrinsics. It outputs compact **3D spatial affordance tokens** representing object poses $\mathbf{T}_{\text{target}}^{\text{world}} \in SE(3)$, surface normal vectors $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$, and collision boundaries.
4. **Station 4 (Latent World Model and State Estimation):** Rather than predicting uncompressed raw pixels, a latent predictive world model (such as a Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture) filters sensory noise, maintains dynamic coordinate frame trees, and tracks internal belief state while bounding spatial uncertainty ($\sigma_{\text{pos}}(t)$).
5. **Station 5 (Semantic Deliberation and Intent Leases):** Operating at a deliberate cadence ($1\text{ Hz}$), a multimodal Vision-Language Model (VLM) reasons over spatial tokens and task goals, emitting an **Expiring Intent Lease** ($\mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}}$):
   $$\mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}} = \left\langle \mathbf{T}_{\text{target}} \in SE(3), \; \mathcal{B}_{\text{workspace}}, \; \|\mathbf{v}\|_{\text{max}}, \; t_{\text{issue}}, \; \Delta t_{\text{TTL}} \right\rangle$$
   This lease bounds the geometric workspace and maximum velocity, granting provisional authority that automatically lapses after $\Delta t_{\text{TTL}}$ unless renewed.
6. **Station 6 (Trajectory Decoding and Action Chunking):** An intermediate diffusion policy or Action Chunking Transformer (ACT) consumes the active intent lease and joint proprioception, generating an action chunk of $H$ future waypoints ($\mathbf{A}_{t:t+H}$) spanning $0.5\text{ to } 1.0\text{ seconds}$ of physical trajectory.
7. **Station 7 (Real-Time Safety Reflex):** Running deterministically at $1000\text{ Hz}$ on a bare-metal microcontroller, the safety supervisor evaluates candidate setpoints against Control Barrier Functions, auditing stopping distances ($d_{\text{stop}} \le d_{\text{clear}}$) and jerk limits ($\|\dddot{\mathbf{q}}\| \le \dddot{q}_{\text{max}}$).
8. **Station 8 (Actuation and Physical Mutation):** Permitted torque setpoints ($u_t$) modulate motor inverter gate drivers, building magnetic flux across stator winding inductance and moving physical linkages ($W_t \to W_{t+1}$).
9. **Station 9 (Endogenous Sensory Feedback):** The displaced mechanism alters the physical environment into state $W_{t+1}$, which immediately generates the subsequent sensory observation stream $O_{t+1}$, closing the causal loop.

### Row 1 (Perceive): Spatial Grounding and 3D Affordance Tokens

The primary responsibility of perception is **spatial grounding**: converting high-dimensional 2D optical pixel arrays into metric 3D geometric tokens referenced to the robot's physical coordinate frame.

In digital machine learning, object detection returns 2D bounding boxes in pixel coordinates ($[u_{\text{min}}, v_{\text{min}}, u_{\text{max}}, v_{\text{max}}]$). On a physical robot, a 2D bounding box contains no depth, metric orientation, or surface normal information. Attempting to grasp an object based on pixel coordinates alone results in either grasping empty air or colliding with the environment.

Perception in Physical AI transforms raw sensory tensors into **3D Spatial Affordance Tokens** ($o_t \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times D_{\text{token}}}$):

1. **Metric Pose:** A rigid-body transformation matrix $\mathbf{T}_{\text{target}}^{\text{world}} \in SE(3)$ specifying 3D position $\mathbf{p} \in \mathbb{R}^3$ and orientation $\mathbf{R} \in SO(3)$.
2. **Contact Geometry:** Surface normal vectors $\hat{\mathbf{n}} \in \mathbb{R}^3$ and estimated contact friction coefficients $\mu$.
3. **Clearance Boundaries:** Oriented 3D bounding boxes ($OBB \subset \mathbb{R}^3$) defining keep-out zones for collision avoidance.

$$\text{Perceive: } \mathbf{I}_{\text{RGB-D}} \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times W \times 4} \xrightarrow{\quad \text{Vision Transformer Backbone} \quad} \left\{ \mathbf{T}_i \in SE(3), \; \hat{\mathbf{n}}_i, \; \mathcal{B}_i \right\}_{i=1}^N$$

*Owning Pipeline Chapter:* **Chapter 4 (Perception)** explores sensor transduction physics, rolling shutter distortion, zero-copy DMA buffers, and memory bus contention.

### Row 2 (Remember): Temporal World Modeling and Dynamic Belief Persistence

Sensors are intermittent, noisy, and subject to line-of-sight occlusions. When a robotic arm reaches for an object, the gripper inevitably occludes the camera's view of the target during the final approach. If an agent relies exclusively on instantaneous observations, it becomes blind at the moment precision is most critical.

The second cognitive dimension is **temporal world modeling**: maintaining an internal belief state ($\mathbf{s}_t$) that preserves knowledge of the physical environment across time, occlusions, and sensor dropouts.

A world model performs three primary functions:

1. **Belief Persistence Under Occlusion:** When an object is occluded, the world model propagates its estimated position forward in time using kinematic motion models, expanding spatial uncertainty bounds with elapsed time:
   $$\sigma_{\text{pos}}(t) = \sigma_0 + \|\mathbf{v}_{\text{target}}\| \cdot \Delta t$$
2. **Coordinate Frame Graph Maintenance:** It tracks the tree of dynamic coordinate transformations ($SE(3)$ frame tree) relating the base frame, camera frames, end-effector, and manipulated objects.
3. **Latent Predictive State Estimation:** Instead of predicting full-resolution future camera frames, modern world models predict compact latent embeddings ($\mathbf{z}_{t+1} = f_{\phi}(\mathbf{z}_t, \mathbf{a}_t)$), reducing computational overhead while capturing physical dynamics.

*Owning Pipeline Chapter:* **Chapter 5 (Memory)** covers $SE(3)$ Lie algebra transformations, frame graph caching, Kalman filtering, and belief uncertainty decay.

### Row 3 (Reason): Semantic Deliberation and Open-World Goal Decomposition

While classical automation relies on hardcoded state machines, Physical AI agents operate in unstructured environments where tasks are specified through natural language. The third cognitive dimension is **semantic deliberation**: parsing human intent, decomposing abstract goals into ordered sub-goals, and resolving environmental ambiguities.

Semantic reasoning is executed by high-capacity multimodal Vision-Language Models running on application processors or edge accelerators:

* **Goal Parsing:** Translating ambiguous prompts (*"Clear the workspace"*) into concrete physical actions (*"Move the blue canister into the recycling bin"*).
* **Affordance Reasoning:** Identifying which physical objects can be grasped, pushed, or assembled based on visual geometry and material properties.
* **Emitting Expiring Intent Leases ($\mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}}$):** Because foundation models are stochastic and non-deterministic, they must never directly command actuator voltages. Instead, System 2 emits a structured, time-bounded **Intent Lease**:
  $$\mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}} = \left\langle \text{GoalID}, \; \mathbf{T}_{\text{target}} \in SE(3), \; \mathcal{B}_{\text{workspace}}, \; \|\mathbf{v}\|_{\text{max}}, \; t_{\text{issue}}, \; \Delta t_{\text{TTL}} \right\rangle$$
  The lease defines where the robot is authorized to operate, clamps its maximum velocity, and sets a strict expiration deadline ($\Delta t_{\text{TTL}} \approx 1000\text{ to } 1500\text{ ms}$). If the reasoning engine crashes, the lease lapses and the system safely holds position.

*Owning Pipeline Chapter:* **Chapter 6 (Reasoning)** investigates open-vocabulary VLM prompting, chain-of-thought planning, intent lease schemas, and lease renewal protocols.

### Row 4 (Plan): Trajectory Generation and Action Chunking

Once an intent lease defines what to accomplish, the agent must determine how to move. The fourth cognitive dimension is **trajectory planning**: translating high-level spatial targets into continuous, collision-free joint trajectories that respect kinematic and dynamic limits.

Modern Physical AI systems deploy **Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT)** and **Diffusion Policies**. Rather than predicting a single joint setpoint for the next time step, the trajectory generator predicts a chunk of $H$ future waypoints in parallel:

$$\mathbf{A}_{t:t+H} = \pi_{\theta}(\mathbf{o}_t, \mathbf{s}_t, \mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}}) = \begin{bmatrix} \mathbf{q}_t & \dot{\mathbf{q}}_t & \mathbf{g}_t \\ \mathbf{q}_{t+1} & \dot{\mathbf{q}}_{t+1} & \mathbf{g}_{t+1} \\ \vdots & \vdots & \vdots \\ \mathbf{q}_{t+H-1} & \dot{\mathbf{q}}_{t+H-1} & \mathbf{g}_{t+H-1} \end{bmatrix}$$

where $\mathbf{q}_k$ represents joint positions, $\dot{\mathbf{q}}_k$ represents joint velocities, and $\mathbf{g}_k$ represents gripper states.

Action chunking provides three key systems advantages:

1. **Delay Amortization:** A single neural inference taking $40\text{ ms}$ generates $800\text{ ms}$ of continuous trajectory ($H=16$ steps at $20\text{ Hz}$), amortizing neural compute delay across continuous physical time.
2. **$\mathcal{C}^2$ Jerk Continuity:** Waypoints are fitted with quintic polynomial splines, guaranteeing continuous second derivatives of acceleration ($\dddot{\mathbf{q}}$) to prevent mechanical shock and gearbox tooth shear.
3. **Temporal Ensembling:** Overlapping action chunks are smoothly blended across a receding horizon, preventing discrete pauses at chunk boundaries.

*Owning Pipeline Chapter:* **Chapter 7 (Planning)** examines diffusion denoising schedules, temporal ensembling, spline interpolation, and lock-free trajectory buffers.

### Row 5 (Execute): Real-Time Reflex and Mathematical Safety Filtering

The final cognitive dimension is **real-time execution and safety enforcement**: converting candidate trajectory waypoints into physical motor phase currents while guaranteeing that physical safety invariants are never breached.

Operating deterministically at $1000\text{ Hz}$ on a dedicated, bare-metal microcontroller, the execution supervisor functions as the **trusted gatekeeper** of the physical machine. It evaluates candidate proposals ($p_t$) against physical constraints using a real-time **Control Barrier Function (CBF) Quadratic Program (QP)**:

$$\begin{aligned}
u_t^* = \arg\min_{u \in \mathcal{U}} \quad & \frac{1}{2} \|u - p_t\|^2 \\
\text{subject to} \quad & L_f h(\mathbf{x}) + L_g h(\mathbf{x}) u + \alpha(h(\mathbf{x})) \ge 0 \\
& d_{\text{stop}}(v) \le d_{\text{clear}} \\
& \|\dot{\boldsymbol{\tau}}\| \le \dot{\tau}_{\text{max}}, \quad I_{\text{winding}} \le I_{\text{thermal}}
\end{aligned}$$

The execution engine guarantees:

1. **Minimal Intervention:** As long as proposed actions are safe ($h(\mathbf{x}) \ge 0$), the optimizer outputs $u_t^* = p_t$ without modification.
2. **Forward Invariance:** If a proposal would drive the mechanism toward collision, joint limits, or over-temperature conditions, the QP minimally modifies the command, projecting it onto the safe boundary $\partial\mathcal{C}$.
3. **Hardware Watchdog Interlocks:** If the application processor fails to refresh its heartbeat ($\tau_{\text{watchdog}} > 20\text{ ms}$), the microcontroller overrides all software, executing an active Category 1 dynamic deceleration halt before asserting Safe Torque Off.

*Owning Pipeline Chapter:* **Chapter 8 (Reflex)** develops bare-metal runtime loops, zero-heap CBF-QP solvers, and hardware emergency braking circuits.

## The Three Cadences: Decoupling Cognitive Speeds Across Silicon

The central dilemma of embodied intelligence is that cognitive operations require vastly different amounts of computational time. Extracting semantic intent from an open-world scene requires billions of operations ($7\text{B}\text{ to } 70\text{B}$ parameter models) taking $500\text{ to } 1500\text{ ms}$. Conversely, maintaining magnetic flux in a brushless motor stator requires Field-Oriented Control loops running at $20\text{ kHz}$ ($50\,\mu\text{s}$), supervised by safety invariant filters running at $1000\text{ Hz}$ ($1.0\text{ ms}$).

Attempting to run these workloads in a single synchronous loop leads to multi-rate timing collapse. Physical AI systems resolve this by decoupling execution into **Three Distinct Temporal Cadences** (@fig-three-cadences):

![The Three Cadences of Physical AI. The asynchronous multi-rate temporal hierarchy: System 2 ($0.5\text{ to } 2\text{ Hz}$ Semantic Intent), System 1.5 ($20\text{ to } 50\text{ Hz}$ Action Chunking), and System 1 ($1000\text{ Hz}$ Real-Time Safety Reflex).](figures/fig03_three_cadences.svg){#fig-three-cadences width=100%}

### 1. System 2 (Slow Cadence · $0.5\text{ to } 2\text{ Hz}$): Semantic Deliberation

* **Role:** High-level cognitive reasoning, open-vocabulary prompt decomposition, and topological task planning.
* **Silicon Substrate:** Multi-core Application Processor (ARM Cortex-A / x86-64) paired with a high-capacity Neural Processing Unit (NPU) or cloud offload.
* **Operating System:** Embedded Linux (Ubuntu / Yocto with `PREEMPT_RT` patch).
* **Workload Characteristics:** Large multimodal foundation models ($7\text{B}\text{ to } 70\text{B}$ weights) with deep key-value attention caches; execution time varies from $400\text{ to } 1500\text{ ms}$.
* **Authority Level:** **Untrusted Proposal Service.** System 2 has zero direct electrical connection to motor timer registers or gate drivers; it outputs an Expiring Intent Lease ($\mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}}$) written to a shared memory mailbox.
* **Failure Containment:** If System 2 encounters an out-of-memory error or long inference stall, its intent lease expires ($\Delta t > \Delta t_{\text{TTL}}$), causing downstream controllers to smoothly hold position.

### 2. System 1.5 (Medium Cadence · $20\text{ to } 50\text{ Hz}$): Trajectory Decoding

* **Role:** Converting active intent leases and proprioceptive joint states into continuous multi-waypoint trajectory chunks.
* **Silicon Substrate:** Dedicated Edge NPU / GPU accelerator running optimized INT8/FP8 TensorRT runtimes.
* **Operating System:** Linux Real-Time User Space (isolated CPU cores with `SCHED_FIFO` priority).
* **Workload Characteristics:** Compact diffusion policies or Action Chunking Transformers ($50\text{M}\text{ to } 200\text{M}$ weights); inference executes in a deterministic $20\text{ to } 45\text{ ms}$ window.
* **Authority Level:** **Candidate Trajectory Generator.** Emits proposed joint position and velocity vectors into an atomic, lock-free SRAM ring buffer.

### 3. System 1 (Fast Cadence · $1000\text{ Hz}$): Real-Time Reflex and Invariant Gatekeeper

* **Role:** Deterministic safety invariant auditing, dynamic stopping distance calculation, Control Barrier Function projection, and spline interpolation down to $20\text{ kHz}$ FOC motor commutation.
* **Silicon Substrate:** Dedicated Real-Time Microcontroller (ARM Cortex-M4/M7 or RISC-V) running on a separate power and clock domain.
* **Operating System:** Bare-Metal Runtime or FreeRTOS with strictly **zero dynamic heap allocation** (`malloc`/`free` forbidden after boot).
* **Workload Characteristics:** Analytical algebraic equations, matrix kinematics, and small quadratic program solvers executing in under $400\,\mu\text{s}$ per $1.0\text{ ms}$ tick ($\text{jitter} \le 15\,\mu\text{s}$).
* **Authority Level:** **Sole Hardware Permission Authority.** The MCU holds exclusive physical control over motor inverter PWM compare registers and hardware gate-driver enable pins.
* **Failure Containment:** If candidate proposals violate physical boundaries or if inter-processor communication drops, the MCU autonomously executes an active Category 1 dynamic braking sequence.

| Dimension | System 2: Deliberation | System 1.5: Trajectory | System 1: Real-Time Reflex |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Cadence** | $0.5\text{ to } 2\text{ Hz}$ ($500\text{ to } 2000\text{ ms}$) | $20\text{ to } 50\text{ Hz}$ ($20\text{ to } 50\text{ ms}$) | $1000\text{ Hz}$ ($1.0\text{ ms} \pm 5\,\mu\text{s}$) |
| **Silicon** | ARM Cortex-A / Host NPU | Edge NPU / Tensor Core | Bare-Metal Cortex-M / RISC-V |
| **Operating System** | Linux (`PREEMPT_RT`) | Linux User Space (`SCHED_FIFO`) | Bare-Metal / FreeRTOS |
| **Memory Model** | Dynamic Virtual Memory / Heap | Pinned Paged Memory | **Zero Heap (Static SRAM Only)** |
| **Workload** | Multimodal VLM ($7\text{B}\text{ to } 70\text{B}$) | Diffusion / ACT ($50\text{M}\text{ to } 200\text{M}$) | CBF-QP Solver / Stopping / FOC |
| **Output Artifact** | Expiring Intent Lease ($\mathcal{L}$) | Trajectory Chunk $\mathbf{A}_{t:t+H}$ | Permitted PWM Duty ($u_t^*$) |
| **Privilege Tier** | **Untrusted Advisory Proposal** | **Candidate Proposal Generator** | **Sole Gatekeeper (PWM Locks)** |
| **Interface** | Shared DRAM IPC Mailbox | Lock-Free SRAM Ring Buffer | Memory-Mapped Registers |
| **Failure Action** | Timeout triggers position hold | Discard chunk and replan | Category 1 Deceleration to STO |

: Comparison of the Three Cadences. Substrates, memory models, privilege tiers, and failure containment across temporal tiers. {#tbl-three-cadences}

## The Great Conflict: When Agent Deliberation Meets Physical Dynamics

Physical AI emerges from the collision of two engineering domains operating under opposing physical and computational realities (@fig-great-tension):

![The Fundamental Tug-of-War in Physical AI. The structural conflict between the AI Deliberation Realm (which demands time, tokens, and compute capacity) and the Physical Dynamics Realm (which demands microsecond speed, deterministic reflexes, and fresh evidence). Physical AI reconciles this conflict through three architectural contracts: the Proposal and Permission split, Action Chunking, and Expiring Leases.](figures/fig03_great_tension.svg){#fig-great-tension width=100%}

### The Two Opposing Forces

1. **The AI Deliberation Realm (The "Brain"):**
   * **Target Capacity:** Large expressive capacity, deep parameter counts ($7\text{B}\text{ to } 70\text{B}$ foundation models), multi-view spatial attention, and iterative diffusion denoising ($10\text{ to } 100$ steps).
   * **Temporal Reality:** Deliberation benefits from additional computation time. Pausing to evaluate chain-of-thought tokens yields higher accuracy and better reasoning.
   * **Operational Requirement:** Demands asynchronous computation decoupled from the real-time physical actuator clock.

2. **The Physical Dynamics Realm (The "Body"):**
   * **Target Determinism:** Microsecond determinism, bounded phase lag, and strict adherence to Newton's laws of motion.
   * **Temporal Reality:** The physical universe never pauses for computation. Gravity acts continuously at $9.81\text{ m/s}^2$; kinetic momentum ($\mathbf{p} = m\mathbf{v}$) carries mass forward; information freshness decays instantly ($\sigma_{\text{pos}} = \sigma_0 + v\Delta t$); and motor coils require high-frequency PWM switching.
   * **Operational Requirement:** Demands guaranteed sub-millisecond execution deadlines ($1\text{ ms}$) without exception.

### The Three Architectural Peace Treaties

Physical AI reconciles this tension through **Three Formal Architectural Contracts**:

1. **The Proposal and Permission Privilege Boundary:** Stochastic, unverified neural models are isolated from physical power electronics. The Linux application processor functions as an untrusted proposal engine, while a deterministic $1000\text{ Hz}$ microcontroller acts as the sole permission authority.
2. **Action Chunking Delay Amortization:** Rather than predicting single discrete steps, the policy predicts a continuous trajectory horizon of $H$ future waypoints ($\mathbf{A}_{t:t+H}$). While the microcontroller smoothly executes waypoints $1 \dots k$, the neural accelerator computes the subsequent chunk in the background, amortizing inference latency across physical time.
3. **Expiring Intent Leases ($\mathcal{L}_{\text{intent}}$) and Hardware Watchdogs:** All high-level authority is time-bounded. If the application processor crashes, freezes, or encounters memory bus starvation, the intent lease expires and the hardware watchdog timer ($\tau_{\text{watchdog}} \le 20\text{ ms}$) trips, triggering an autonomous, MCU-driven Category 1 dynamic deceleration halt.

### How to Read an Uneven Grid

An engineering matrix is rarely uniform, and the empty entries carry as much architectural information as the full ones:

* **Non-Binding Cells:** Semantic reasoning commands no motor torque directly, so mechanical torque rate limits do not reach it. Similarly, perception algorithms do not drive mechanical gearboxes. Recognizing which constraints do not bind a given stage allows engineers to focus safety enforcement where it is mathematically necessary.
* **Universal vs. Local Constraints:** Thermal dissipation (Column 4) reaches every row because heat is produced by sensors, processors, and motor windings alike. In contrast, mechanical actuation limits (Column 3) reach only the stages that generate motion commands (Plan and Execute).

![The Physical AI Curriculum Blueprint and Roadmap. Tracing the progression from Part I foundations through the Part II sensory-motor organs to Part III integration, governance, and release qualification.](figures/fig03_modular_blueprint.svg){#fig-modular-blueprint width=100%}

## Systems Fallacies and Pitfalls

::: {.callout-warning}
### Common Engineering Fallacies in Embodied Cognition
* **Fallacy 1: The Monolithic Frequency Fallacy.**  
  *The Fallacy:* With sufficient compute scaling, a 70B parameter Vision-Language-Action foundation model can execute directly at $1000\text{ Hz}$, eliminating the need for multi-rate hierarchies.  
  *The Reality:* Even if compute latency reached zero, optical exposure time ($8\text{ to } 15\text{ ms}$) and motor coil electrical rise time ($\tau_e = L/R$, $5\text{ to } 15\text{ ms}$) impose fundamental physical limits that digital compute scaling cannot bypass.
* **Fallacy 2: The Infinite Horizon Fallacy.**  
  *The Fallacy:* If an action chunk horizon of $H=16$ steps is effective, then $H=256$ steps is sixteen times better because it amortizes inference delay across several seconds.  
  *The Reality:* Long action chunk horizons operate open-loop with respect to new environmental observations. If an obstacle enters the workspace during an unrolling chunk, the robot continues executing its pre-computed trajectory. Chunk horizons must be bounded by physical information freshness: $H \cdot \Delta t_{\text{step}} \le \tau_{\text{world}}$.
* **Fallacy 3: The Software Timestamp Illusion.**  
  *The Fallacy:* Multi-rate vision, planning, and control loops can be synchronized using user-space software timestamps (`time.time()`).  
  *The Reality:* Operating system thread preemption and memory bus contention introduce $10\text{ to } 40\text{ ms}$ of non-deterministic timing jitter. Microsecond synchronization requires hardware IEEE 1588 PTP clocks and timer capture registers.
:::

## Summary and What Comes Next

In Part I, we have established the physical and architectural foundations of embodied intelligence:

1. **Chapter 1 (The Causal Boundary):** Software moves matter; physical momentum ($\mathbf{p} = m\mathbf{v}$) and Joule heat ($I^2 R$) cannot be undone with `try/catch`; stochastic neural models must be isolated from motor inverters via the Proposal and Permission boundary.
2. **Chapter 2 (The Physical Constraints):** The universe sets the clock; sensory information decays upon transduction; tail latency distributions ($P_{99}$) govern dynamic stopping distance ($d_{\text{stop}}$); and pipelining must prioritize information freshness over throughput.
3. **Chapter 3 (The Cognitive Dimensions):** Deconstructed the five cognitive work dimensions (Perceive, Remember, Reason, Plan, Execute); established the Three Cadences of intelligence across heterogeneous silicon; resolved the compute-versus-physics conflict through three architectural contracts; and constructed the Physical AI Co-Design Matrix.

### Entering Part II: The Agent Architecture

With Part I complete, we now possess the foundational principles. In **Part II (Chapters 4 through 8)**, we examine the Co-Design Matrix row by row, systematically constructing, isolating, and validating each of the **Five Canonical Sensory-Motor Organs** across the Proposal and Permission boundary: starting with **Perception and Spatial Tokenization** in Chapter 4.
